roleplay.personas.cold_lead.brief: Kevin Brooks asked about homes three months ago and stopped answering.
roleplay.personas.cold_lead.lines.0: Oh, hi. Sorry, I've been really busy. I'm not sure we're still looking.
roleplay.personas.cold_lead.lines.1: We kind of put it on hold. The market felt crazy.
roleplay.personas.cold_lead.lines.2: I don't want to waste your time if we're not ready.
roleplay.personas.cold_lead.lines.3: Maybe in the spring? I don't know yet.
roleplay.personas.cold_lead.lines.lost: I'll reach out when we're ready. Thanks.
roleplay.personas.cold_lead.lines.won: Sure, send me a few homes and let's talk next Tuesday.
roleplay.personas.cold_lead.name: Lead who went quiet
roleplay.personas.commission_pushback.br: Dan Ortiz likes you but another agent offered a lower commission.
roleplay.personas.commission_pushback.li: I like you, but another agent said they'd do it for a lot less. Can you match that?
At the end of the day, isn't every agent putting it on the MLS anyway?
What do I actually get for the extra money?
I'd still feel better if you came down a little.
I'll probably go with the cheaper option. No hard feelings.
Fair enough, I can see the difference. Let's get the paperwork started.
roleplay.personas.downsizing_couple.brie: Ruth and Carl Moreno are selling the family home in Sugar Land to move somewhere smaller.
roleplay.personas.downsizing_couple.line: We raised our kids in this house. Selling it is hard, and we don't even know where we'd go next.
What if it sells before we find our next place? We can't be left without a home.
Do we really have to fix everything before we list? We're not up for a big project.
Our neighbor's house took five months to sell. Why would ours be any different?
We need some time to talk about it. We'll be in touch.
That helps a lot. Let's set a time next week to plan it step by step.
roleplay.personas.downsizing_couple.name: Couple downsizing after 30 years
roleplay.personas.expired.brief: Greg Hall's listing just expired after 120 days with another agent.
roleplay.personas.expired.lines.0: Let me guess, another agent calling now that my listing expired. Why should I talk to you?
roleplay.personas.expired.lines.1: The last agent promised a lot too. Nothing happened in four months.
roleplay.personas.expired.lines.2: Are you just going to tell me to lower the price?
roleplay.personas.expired.lines.3: I'm tired of this. Why would it be different with you?
roleplay.personas.expired.lines.lost: I think I'll take the house off the market for a while.
roleplay.personas.expired.lines.won: Fine, I'll give you twenty minutes. Come by tomorrow at five.
roleplay.personas.expired.name: Expired listing
roleplay.personas.fsbo.brief: Linda Park is selling her own home to save the commission.
roleplay.personas.fsbo.lines.0: Hello? If you're an agent, I'm selling the house myself, thanks.
roleplay.personas.fsbo.lines.1: I've already had people come by. Why would I pay a commission?
roleplay.personas.fsbo.lines.2: I can put it online myself. What would you do that I can't?
roleplay.personas.fsbo.lines.3: Maybe. But I'm not signing anything today.
roleplay.personas.fsbo.lines.lost: I'll keep trying on my own for now. Bye.
roleplay.personas.fsbo.lines.won: Okay, you can come by Saturday morning and walk me through it.
roleplay.personas.fsbo.name: Selling without an agent
roleplay.personas.interviewing_seller.br: Mark Ellis is selling a four-bedroom home in Katy and meeting three agents this week.
roleplay.personas.interviewing_seller.li: Thanks for coming. I'm talking to three agents this week, so tell me: why should I list with you?
Another agent told me we could get 30,000 dollars more than your number. Why is your price lower?
How exactly will you market the house? I don't want it sitting for months.
This all sounds good, but I still want to think it over after the other two meetings.
Thanks for your time. I'll call you after I've met the others.
All right, you've made a good case. Let's meet Thursday and go over the listing agreement.
roleplay.personas.low_appraisal.brief: Sara Nguyen's buyer's appraisal came in 15,000 dollars under the contract price.
roleplay.personas.low_appraisal.lines.0: The appraisal came in 15,000 dollars under our price. What happens now? Is the deal falling apart?
roleplay.personas.low_appraisal.lines.1: I'm not just dropping my price by 15,000. That's not fair to me.
roleplay.personas.low_appraisal.lines.2: Can we fight the appraisal? It feels wrong.
roleplay.personas.low_appraisal.lines.3: What are my real options here, and what would you do?
roleplay.personas.low_appraisal.lines.lo: I need to think about whether I want to keep this buyer at all.
roleplay.personas.low_appraisal.lines.wo: Okay, I feel better. Let's go ahead with the plan you laid out.
roleplay.personas.low_appraisal.name: Appraisal came in low
roleplay.personas.rate_worried_buyer.bri: Jasmine Cole is a first-time buyer in Houston thinking of waiting a year.
roleplay.personas.rate_worried_buyer.lin: Honestly, with rates where they are, I'm thinking of waiting a year before I buy.
But my monthly payment would be so much higher than my rent. How is that a good idea?
What if rates drop right after I buy? Then I'd feel stuck.
I'm still not sure. What would you actually suggest I do next?
I think I'll wait and see what rates do. Thanks anyway.
Okay, that makes sense. Let's talk to a lender and look at a few homes this weekend.
